verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Every symbol of (4.1) is in the Lean, but three of them in a rewritten encoding. (i) A = 1/2+h, D = 1/2-h, d = 1-η², L = 1-2hη² and X = s/q are literal definitions (CoordinateAlgebra.A/D/d/L, SimilarityProfile.X, the latter on a PhysicalPoint p = (t,(s,z)) so that p.2.1 is s). (ii) The paper's pair "z = q^D η, τ = q(1-η²)" is encoded the other way round: SimilarityCoordinates defines q as the unique positive root of τ = q - z²q^a with a = 2h, and then η := z / q^{(1-a)/2}. Recovery: (1-a)/2 = (1-2h)/2 = D (SimilarityProfile.D_eq), so η = z/q^D is z = q^D η for q > 0; substituting that into τ = q - z²q^{2h} and using q^{2D}q^{2h} = q^{2D+2h} = q (as 2D+2h = 1) gives τ = q(1-η²). Both halves of that rewriting are theorems already in the repository: CoordinateAlgebra.forward_coordinate_identity and SimilarityCoordinates.tau_coordinate_identity. (iii) τ = 1-t is not a named definition: it is substituted inline, as `1 - p.1` in SimilarityProfile.q and as the first component of BaseChartJets.physicalInput. (iv) s = r²/2 likewise: the similarity/profile layer treats s as a primitive coordinate (the SimilarityProfile module header records "The physical variables are (t,s,z), with s = r²/2"), and the substitution s = r²/2 is made where the physical Cartesian or cylindrical point enters, by AxisymmetricFields.radialEnergy = (x₀²+x₁²)/2 and ActualBaseResidual.profilePoint_chart. (v) The range 0 < h < 1/2 is not one declaration; it is carried as the hypothesis pair (hh : 0 < h) (hh1 : h < 1/2), equivalently 0 < a < 1 for a = 2h in SimilarityCoordinates, on each theorem that needs it (SimilarityProfile.q_pos, CoordinateAlgebra.D_pos). The exponents, signs, the factor 2 in L and in s, and the h-range all match the page term for term; no constant or exponent differs.
